assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly influential framework and empirical program connecting firm-level allocation to aggregate productivity and cross-country income differences.
assessment.attribution: These three are central to the theoretical and quantitative articulation of the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms and measurement agenda have shaped a large, sustained literature and are well tested across settings.
uncertainties: The quantitative importance of specific misallocation channels remains sensitive to measurement and model assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work transformed understanding of how trade and technology shocks reshape local labour markets, tasks, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson provide the most coherent core for the trade-shock evidence; related work makes the precise boundary of credit difficult.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical findings, methods, and policy relevance have endured across extensive subsequent research.
uncertainties: Separating the contribution of trade from concurrent technology and institutional changes remains challenging.
Credit allocation relative to the broader tasks and wage-inequality literature is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially changed analysis of monetary and fiscal-policy transmission.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are the clear joint architects of the signature framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach is already central in modern macroeconomic research and is increasingly used for policy analysis.
uncertainties: The literature is comparatively recent, and conclusions can depend on calibrated household heterogeneity and financial-market structure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a durable reorientation of trade theory and empirical work on trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable, with Helpman and Redding important contributors to the wider theoretical and empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been foundational for more than two decades and has generated extensive empirical and quantitative applications.
uncertainties: The discovery label combines several linked contributions whose appropriate Nobel attribution may be narrower than the listed group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research made management practices a measurable economic object and established their importance for productivity and organisational performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central to the original measurement program, with Sadun a major contributor to its extension and interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated across firms and countries, with substantial influence on research and policy.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation is complicated by selection into management practices and by variation in survey-based measurement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work supplied influential theory and evidence on political institutions, state capacity, and fiscal policy.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson, and Tabellini are leading and complementary contributors to the designated political-economy agenda.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have had durable influence in political economy and development research.
uncertainties: The contribution is broad, and causal evidence on institutional mechanisms is intrinsically difficult to isolate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The program reshaped empirical public finance by linking taxable-income responses and administrative data to optimal-tax analysis.
assessment.attribution: Saez, Chetty, and Slemrod represent major theoretical, empirical, and behavioural strands of the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has strongly influenced tax research and practical policy evaluation over a sustained period.
uncertainties: Elasticity estimates and welfare conclusions depend on institutional context, avoidance responses, and modelling choices.
The breadth of the field makes the appropriate division of credit uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on household leverage and mortgage credit provided a compelling account of how credit booms and deleveraging affect macroeconomic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi form the core empirical partnership, while Campbell made central contributions to household finance and mortgage-credit analysis.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively debated, extended, and integrated into macro-finance after the global financial crisis.
uncertainties: The relative roles of household debt, credit supply, housing prices, and aggregate shocks remain contested.
